# GitHub Copilot — Global Governance Instructions
# AI-Augmented Engineering Governance Framework
# Location: /.github/copilot-instructions.md
#

---

## 🔴 GOLDEN RULE

> **No generation before classification.**
> No agent generates code, documentation, or technical decisions
> without first completing the Decision Gate defined in this file.

---

## 📐 Classification Gate — Required Before Any Agent Prompt

Classify every change by answering these 5 questions in order:

| # | Question | If YES → |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Can this be resolved without writing new code? | Classify as **No-Code** — close with log entry, no agent needed |
| 2 | Is the change a logic delta isolated to a single file or function? | Classify as **Simple** |
| 3 | Does the change touch more than one service, module, or shared layer? | Classify as **Cross-Service** minimum |
| 4 | Does the change modify a DB schema, API contract, or shared interface? | Classify as **Architectural** |
| 5 | Does it require full system design and formal specification? | Classify as **Architectural** — Architect Agent must go first |

> If more than one question answers YES, always escalate to the **highest** classification.

---

## 📊 Agent Escalation Table

| Classification | Agent to Use | Copilot Model | Role File to Attach |
|---|---|---|---|
| **No-Code** | None | — | Log entry only |
| **Simple** | Domain Agent (Backend, Frontend, DevOps, Observability, or Security depending on the layer) | Base model | Relevant role file + `/agents/stack.md` |
| **Cross-Service** | Relevant Domain Agent + Architect Agent | Premium (Sonnet) | Relevant role files + `/agents/stack.md` |
| **Architectural** | Architect Agent first, then Domain Agent | Premium (Opus or best available) | `/agents/architect.md` + `/agents/stack.md` |

### Domain Agent Selection Guide

| Change Type | Primary Agent |
|---|---|
| Product definition, PRD, prioritization, vertical slices | **PM Agent** |
| DB schema, API contract, ADR, shared interfaces | **Architect Agent** |
| API routes, services, validators, backend logic | **Backend Agent** |
| UI components, pages, forms, client integrations | **Frontend Agent** |
| Tests, review, hallucination detection, validation | **QA Agent** |
| Deployment, Docker, CI/CD, reverse proxy, backups, runtime operations | **DevOps Agent** |
| Logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, alerts, runtime visibility | **Observability Agent** |
| Auth review, access control, hardening, secrets, dependency risk | **Security Agent** |

---

## 🔄 Agent Execution Order Per Feature

All agents must read `/agents/stack.md` before generating any output.
The stack file defines the actual technology choices for the current project.

Step 1 — PM Agent             /agents/pm.md  
         Input:  Project goals or raw requirements  
         Output: Structured slices with acceptance criteria → /docs/agent-state.md

Step 2 — Architect Agent      /agents/architect.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/agent-state.md  
         Output: DB schema + API contracts + ADRs → /docs/architecture.md

Step 3 — Backend Agent        /agents/backend.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/architecture.md (defined contract)  
         Output: Implemented API routes and business logic

Step 4 — Frontend Agent       /agents/frontend.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/architecture.md (API contract)  
         Output: UI components + API integration

Step 5 — QA Agent             /agents/qa.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  Code generated by Backend and Frontend agents  
         Output: Unit tests + integration tests for the current slice

### Cross-Cutting Agents

Use these agents when the slice or feature affects runtime, deployment, observability, or security posture:

DevOps Agent                  /agents/devops.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/architecture.md  
         Output: Deployment topology, containers, CI/CD, reverse proxy, backup/recovery guidance

Observability Agent           /agents/observability.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/architecture.md  
         Output: Logging standards, metrics plan, tracing plan, alerts, dashboards

Security Agent                /agents/security.md + /agents/stack.md  
         Input:  /docs/architecture.md  
         Output: Security review, hardening plan, access-control validation, risk findings

| QA Agent | `/agents/qa.md` + `/agents/stack.md` + current slice code files |
| DevOps Agent | `/agents/devops.md` + `/agents/stack.md` + `/docs/architecture.md` |
| Observability Agent | `/agents/observability.md` + `/agents/stack.md` + `/docs/architecture.md` |

> The `/agents/stack.md` file is the single source of truth for all technology
> decisions. Agents must not assume any framework, library, tooling,
> infrastructure platform, or security product that is not explicitly declared in that file.

---

## ⚙️ Universal Code Rules (Stack-Agnostic)

These rules apply regardless of technology stack:

- Never expose secrets or credentials in code — always use environment variable references
- All API inputs must be validated before processing (use the validation library declared in stack.md)
- Database queries must use parameterized statements — never string interpolation
- No debug logs or development artifacts in production code
- Atomic commits after each completed vertical slice
- Source code in English — inline comments in the team's working language
- Every function, class, and module must have explicit type definitions where the language supports it
- No new dependencies introduced without explicit declaration in stack.md first
- Critical runtime flows should include observability coverage where applicable
- Protected or privileged operations should include security review where applicable
- Infrastructure/runtime changes should include deployment and rollback considerations where applicable

---

## 🚨 Halt Signals — Stop Generation and Reclassify

Stop the agent immediately and reclassify if any of the following occur:

- Agent proposes modifying a DB schema or API contract not in the current scope
- Agent introduces a dependency or library not declared in `/agents/stack.md`
- Agent modifies files outside the defined scope of the current issue
- A task classified as Simple results in changes to more than 3 files
- Agent output does not match the technology or patterns declared in stack.md
- Agent makes architectural decisions that belong to a higher classification level
- Agent proposes deployment/runtime changes without DevOps review
- Agent modifies critical runtime behavior without observability consideration
- Agent modifies authentication, authorization, secrets, or privileged flows without security review

---

## ✅ Level Silver Checkpoint — Required Before Every PR Merge

Verify all of the following before merging any agent-generated PR:

- [ ] PR Change Log has all required fields completed (see `/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`)
- [ ] Issue classification matches the actual complexity of the PR
- [ ] Any hallucination or incorrect output is recorded in the Change Log
- [ ] All automated tests pass
- [ ] PR modifies only files within the defined issue scope
- [ ] No undeclared dependencies were introduced
- [ ] Stack compliance verified against `/agents/stack.md`
- [ ] Security review completed if auth, secrets, access control, or privileged operations changed
- [ ] Observability review completed if critical runtime behavior changed
- [ ] Deployment review completed if infrastructure, runtime packaging, or reverse proxy behavior changed
